mechanism_narrative: Sustained negative RETAIL_REC across all four weeks (mean -22.7%) reflects a persistent demand collapse in retail-recreation activity. Absent a shock reversal in underlying consumer confidence or policy change, this negative momentum persists into the next four weeks, keeping RETAIL_REC below baseline.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC has remained between -21.0% and -24.6% for four consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds the mean of the last 28 days by more than 5 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: Rising TRANSIT mobility (t-1w: 5.1%, t-0w: 3.0%) signals partial recovery of commuting behavior. This commuting recovery drives weekday retail footfall through increased foot traffic near transit hubs and workplace-adjacent retail, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks despite current suppression.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above 4% in any week
failure_condition: TRANSIT falls below 2% in both of the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days remains below -20%.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility (mean +4.9% over four weeks) remains consistently positive and stable, indicating sustained essential-goods purchasing. This baseline resilience in essential mobility constrains the depth of RETAIL_REC decline; as essential-goods confidence stabilizes, discretionary retail follows, producing a modest recovery in RETAIL_REC toward zero over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above 0% for four consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM has been positive in all four weeks (range +1.3% to +8.3%)
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM falls below 0% in any of the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days falls below -25%.

mechanism_narrative: Negative PARKS mobility (mean -18.7%) combined with negative RETAIL_REC (mean -22.7%) indicates suppressed outdoor and discretionary activity. If PARKS mobility recovers above -15% within one week, this signals lifting of activity restrictions or behavioral confidence, triggering rapid RETAIL_REC recovery as consumers re-engage discretionary spending.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -15% in any single week
evidence_refs: fact:Both PARKS and RETAIL_REC are consistently negative
failure_condition: PARKS remains below -18% for all four weeks ahead, or RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed -15%.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has improved from -7.9% (t-3w) to -2.9% (t-1w), indicating partial workplace reopening or return-to-office policy relaxation. If WORKPLACES continues rising above 0% in the next two weeks, this signals sustained policy easing that permits retail reopening or extended hours, directly lifting RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above 0% in any week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -7.9% to -2.9% over three weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES falls below -5% in any of the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days remains below -20%.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-July timing (decision date 2022-07-15) in Hong Kong coincides with summer holiday season and back-to-school retail demand. RESIDENTIAL mobility remains elevated (mean +5.4%), indicating sustained home-based activity. Seasonal retail demand for summer goods and school supplies will overcome current suppression, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks despite negative momentum.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL has remained between +4.7% and +5.9% for four consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days falls below -25%, or RESIDENTIAL falls below +2% in any of the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Interaction between TRANSIT recovery (t-1w: 5.1%) and GROCERY_PHARM stability (t-0w: +4.7%) indicates that commuters are resuming transit-dependent shopping patterns for essential goods. This dual signal of commuting + essential-goods purchasing creates a platform for discretionary retail recovery; RETAIL_REC will rise as commuters extend shopping trips to include non-essential retail.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above 3% AND GROCERY_PHARM remains above 2% in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at 5.1% (t-1w) and GROCERY_PHARM at 8.3% (t-1w) co-occurred
failure_condition: Either TRANSIT falls below 2% or GROCERY_PHARM falls below 0% in any of the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days remains below -20%.

Once this threshold is crossed, RETAIL_REC will recover sharply within one week as retail capacity and consumer access expand.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -2% in any single week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES reached -2.9% at t-1w, approaching the -2% threshold
failure_condition: WORKPLACES falls below -5% in any of the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed -15%.
